messages.text: 'George had perfect position' - Wolff defends Mercedes' Vegas Q3 strategy

metadata.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff dismissed suggestions the team should have done more to aid George Russell's bid for Las Vegas Grand Prix pole as he insisted the British driver had "perfect" track position for his final run in qualifying.
metadata.content: Las Vegas GP: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists George Russell had 'perfect' track position in qualifying amid questions over tow | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Las Vegas GP: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists George Russell had 'perfect' track position in qualifying amid questions over tow Kimi Antonelli was fastest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying but will start from sixth because of a grid penalty; George Russell will start from second after finishing third; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Saturday 21 November 2026 08:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was left shocked after Kimi Antonelli benefitted from tow to go fastest in Las Vegas qualifying Mercedes chief Toto Wolff dismissed suggestions the team should have done more to aid George Russell's bid for Las Vegas Grand Prix pole as he insisted the British driver had "perfect" track position for his final run in qualifying. Russell had gone into the final part of qualifying as the favourite for pole but ultimately finished third after his team-mate Kimi Antonelli topped Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Many had assumed Mercedes would use Antonelli, who has already sealed the Drivers' Championship and is serving a five-place grid penalty in Las Vegas, to give Russell a tow up the main straight to help him in his bid to chase down Verstappen for second in the drivers' standings. messages.text: Antonelli fastest but Verstappen on pole after dramatic Las Vegas qualifying

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a five-place grid penalty means Max Verstappen will start on pole position from George Russell.
metadata.content: Las Vegas GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest but Max Verstappen on pole from George Russell after dramatic qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Las Vegas GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest but Max Verstappen on pole from George Russell after dramatic qualifying Kimi Antonelli was quickest in qualifying but a five-place grid penalty for a new engine means Max Verstappen will be on pole from George Russell for the Las Vegas Grand Prix; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event By Nigel Chiu in Las Vegas Saturday 21 November 2026 05:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a five-place grid penalty means Max Verstappen will start on pole position from George Russell. New Formula 1 world champion Antonelli will start sixth due to a grid penalty for exceeding his internal combustion engine allocation and surprisingly went fastest in a hectic end to Q3. The Mercedes driver only just crossed the line in time to start a final flying lap and was helped by a huge slipstream from the Racing Bulls throughout the lap to beat Verstappen by 0.258s. messages.text: Hamilton 'devastated', Leclerc 'angry' after Ferrari Las Vegas shocker

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc was left "angry" while Lewis Hamilton said he was "devastated" after both Ferrari drivers suffered shock early exits from Las Vegas Grand Prix Qualifying.
metadata.content: Las Vegas GP: Lewis Hamilton 'devastated' and Charles Leclerc 'angry' after both Ferrari drivers make shock early exits from qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Las Vegas GP: Lewis Hamilton 'devastated' and Charles Leclerc 'angry' after both Ferrari drivers make shock early exits from qualifying Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were both eliminated from Q2 during qualifying in Las Vegas; Leclerc will start the race from 10th, with Hamilton a place behind him; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Saturday 21 November 2026 07:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Both Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were eliminated from Q2 as Ferrari were left frustrated in Las Vegas qualifying Charles Leclerc was left "angry" while Lewis Hamilton said he was "devastated" after both Ferrari drivers suffered shock early exits from Las Vegas Grand Prix Qualifying. The Italian team had arrived at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit wary of the challenges the long straights and cold temperatures could pose them, but Friday night's session went far worse than either driver had anticipated. Both drivers were eliminated in Q2 as Leclerc took 11th with Hamilton a place behind him. They will each move a position forward on the grid due to a penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri. messages.text: Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper use

metadata.summary: Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowledge of the use of sandpaper to alter the ball during his side's Test series against South Africa in 2018.
metadata.content: Sandpapergate: Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper use after Cameron Bancroft allegations | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Sandpapergate: Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper use after Cameron Bancroft allegations Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowledge of the use of sandpaper, directly contradicting Cameron Bancroft's claims that the coaching staff were aware of the plot to tamper with the ball; Bancroft named Lehmann as present in the discussions around sandpaper use Noah Langford Sports Journalist Saturday 21 November 2026 08:39, UK Image: Darren Lehmann is currently the coach of Northamptonshire in the County Championship Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowledge of the use of sandpaper to alter the ball during his side's Test series against South Africa in 2018. The development comes after batter Cameron Bancroft - who was caught on camera using sandpaper - exacerbated the Sandpapergate scandal with a 4,000-word statement asserting that the entire team - including the bowling group - knew about the use of sandpaper on the three-Test tour of South Africa in 2018. Bancroft named Lehmann as one of the members present in a discussion around the use of sandpaper, even quoting his former coach in directing an assistant to take the sandpaper from Bancroft once the ball-tampering had been discovered by the TV broadcast. messages.text: Harden moves past Kobe in career 50-point games as Cavs beat Pacers

metadata.summary: James Harden scored 51 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.
metadata.content: NBA: Cleveland Cavaliers' James Harden scores 26th career 50-point game to move past Kobe Bryant in win over Indiana Pacers | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NBA: Cleveland Cavaliers' James Harden scores 26th career 50-point game to move past Kobe Bryant in win over Indiana Pacers James Harden moved past the late Kobe Bryant in career 50-point games as the Cavs beat the Pacers 128-119 ; watch the 2026/27 NBA season - including the Christmas Day games and the NBA finals - on Sky Sports Saturday 21 November 2026 07:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA match between the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Indiana Pacers. James Harden scored 51 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night. It was the 18-year veteran guard's 26th 50-point game, passing the late Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games in NBA history. It was Harden's first since he had 55 points for the Los Angeles Clippers against the Charlotte Hornets on November 22, 2025. Harden is the sixth player to have a 50-point game for Cleveland. It was also his best scoring game with the Cavaliers since being acquired near the trade deadline in February, surpassing the 36 he had against Chicago last season.
